newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Firm punt shdn't stop Irish joining EMU-Schmidhube.
newsitem.headline: Firm punt shdn't stop Irish joining EMU-Schmidhube.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Peter Schmidhuber said on Friday that while the strong position of the Irish pound within the ERM grid was a problem, it should no prevent Ireland from taking part in EMU.
Schmidhuber was in Dublin to give a private briefing to member of the Institute of European affairs.

"That the strong position of the Irish pound is a problem there is no doubt," he told Reuters."On the other hand I cannot see that this problem will prevent Ireland from taking part in EMU." Schmidhuber noted that the ERM fluctation margins had been widened from 2.25 percent to 15 percent in August 1993.
"What this means for the convergence criteria, that has not been decided up 'til now," he said.

The Irish pound has been the strongest currency within the ERM grid in recent months and is currenty trading more 11 percent over the weakest currency in the grid, the french franc. -- Dublin newsroom +353 1 676 9779
